evidence.ai_role: Random Forest, logistic regression, gradient boosting and SVM learn multidomain associations with past-year fall-history strata; feature importance characterizes the internally evaluated profile.
evidence.tested: Stratified five-fold internal classification of fall-history strata in 147 adults, excluding specified post-fall variables.
evidence.unknown: Cross-sectional history, self-report and small uneven strata; no external validation, causal effects or demonstrated future-fall prediction.

organization: Shahid Bahonar University of Kerman; University of Saskatchewan; Sport Science Research Institute

source_review.scope: Primary manuscript Methods, relevant Results, limitations and first-version publication metadata reviewed.

summary: In a cross-sectional study of 147 community-dwelling adults aged 55 and older, machine-learning models classified ordered past-year fall-history groups from physical-function, activity, health and social measures. Random Forest reported four-class accuracy of 0.946 and binary AUC of 0.968 under internal five-fold validation after excluding fall-location, fall-situation and fear-of-falling variables. The preprint describes associations with recorded fall history, not prediction of future falls. A small, imbalanced single-region sample and self-reported measures limit generalization; external and prospective validation remain necessary.
title: Machine learning links multidomain profiles to fall history
